SINGLE_LANDCOVER.split_note: BigEarthNet official test shard (test_p8.hdf5), all 12 bands at native 10 m, checkpoint ckpt_step_107625.pt (gsd_conditioning=True). Uniformly 10 m, so this split measures calibration at native resolution ONLY and cannot show whether confidence stays honest as resolution coarsens - that needs the multi-resolution split.

TEMPORAL_CHANGE_MAP.split_note: LEVIR-CD official test split, 2048 tiles, 1024 pixels sampled per tile, checkpoint ckpt_step_26700.pt. Split for fitting is by TILE, not by pixel, because pixels within a tile are spatially correlated and a pixel-wise split would leak. The head was trained with pos_weight=10.1, so its logits carry a deliberate positive-class offset that temperature scaling alone cannot remove.

_router_intent.split_note: CLEAN_HOLDOUT from satquery/synth/holdout.py, n=29, hand-written and never used to tune the templates. The synthetic bank's own held-out split was NOT used: it measures template memorisation, so a temperature fitted there would be calibrated to a distribution the router never meets.
_router_intent.rejection_reason: only 14 fitting samples, below the 500 needed for a temperature that is not fitted to noise

note: Heads under `rejected` are deliberately left uncalibrated at runtime and keep reporting ece_after = -1.0. A fitted parameter that did not survive its own held-out check is worse than none.
